data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical immunomodulators & antipsoriatics_

**Class:** Vitamin D3 analogues for topical use

## Mechanism of action
- Bind the vitamin D receptor (VDR) → inhibit keratinocyte proliferation, promote normal differentiation; reduce Th17 cytokines (IL-17, IL-8)
- Do not cause skin atrophy

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic plaque psoriasis (first-line, especially with steroid: calcipotriol + betamethasone dipropionate gel/ointment/foam), scalp psoriasis, nail psoriasis
- Off-label: vitiligo (with phototherapy), morphoea, disorders of keratinisation (ichthyoses, Darier), prurigo nodularis, seborrhoeic keratoses

## Dose & formulations
- Calcipotriol 0.005% twice daily (maximum 100 g/week adults; 50 g/week for children 6–12, 75 g/week for 12+)
- Tacalcitol 4 µg/g once daily; calcitriol 3 µg/g twice daily (less irritating — face/flexures)
- Calcipotriol + betamethasone once daily for 4 weeks, then as needed/twice weekly

## Adverse effects
- Local irritation (lesional and perilesional), especially on face and flexures (calcipotriol)
- Hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria if maximum weekly dose is exceeded or in renal disease
- Photosensitivity is not typical, but UVA degrades calcipotriol — apply after phototherapy, not before

## Contraindications
- Disorders of calcium metabolism, severe renal/hepatic disease, generalised pustular/erythrodermic psoriasis (large areas)

## Drug interactions
- Salicylic acid inactivates calcipotriol — do not mix
- Thiazides/calcium supplements: hypercalcaemia risk

## Monitoring
- Serum calcium if near maximum dose or with renal disease

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data — use small areas if needed.

## Viva points
- Calcipotriol maximum 100 g/week
- Inactivated by salicylic acid and UVA
- Combination with betamethasone improves efficacy and reduces irritation

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.49 (Topical vitamin D3); Khopkar ch.23 (Topical calcipotriol). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
